assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing item operations, coupon logic, total calculation, and checkout.
assertions.evidence: Five @TableTest methods: addsItemsFromTheCatalogue, removesItemsFromTheCart, appliesCouponsToTheCart, checksOutTheCart, calculatesTheCartTotal.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Add item table has 6 rows covering accumulation, unknown product, zero/negative qty; no coupon/stock cross-multiplication present.

assertions.text: Item operations (add/remove), coupon application (validity and replacement), cart total calculation (coupon type effects on price), and checkout (stock verification) are in separate @TableTest methods.
assertions.evidence: addsItemsFromTheCatalogue, removesItemsFromTheCart, appliesCouponsToTheCart, calculatesTheCartTotal, checksOutTheCart are all separate methods.

assertions.text: Each table row is independently executable — no row depends on a prior row's result.
assertions.evidence: Each row specifies 'Cart Before', 'Active Coupon Before', 'Cart Items', etc. as explicit inputs, not derived from prior rows.

assertions.text: Coupon application table uses before/after columns to specify the state change.
assertions.evidence: Columns 'Active Coupon Before | Coupon Code | Coupon In Store | Active Coupon After?' in appliesCouponsToTheCart.

assertions.text: Coupon application table tests validity and replacement — not coupon type effects on price.
assertions.evidence: appliesCouponsToTheCart asserts success/message/activeCouponAfter only, no discount amount computed; calculatesTheCartTotal handles price effects separately.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Message?', 'Total?', 'Active coupon after?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Cart After?, Success?, Message?, Cart After?, Success?, Message?, Active Coupon After?, Success?, Message?, Success?, Message Mentions?, Total?

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions — not outcomes.
assertions.evidence: 'Add new item to empty cart', 'Insufficient stock by one unit', 'Apply a percentage coupon with none active' describe conditions.

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — not code identifiers like 'productId', 'result'.
assertions.evidence: Columns like 'Catalogue', 'Cart Before', 'Quantity', 'Success?', 'Message?' though 'Product Id' is a minor nit noted as non-weighted.

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 5 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 5 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method applies one uniform assertion pattern to every row — not different assertions per scenario. Several unconditional assertions checking distinct observable outputs of one result (e.g. success, message, resulting cart) count as one uniform pattern; the anti-pattern is branching on the row (if/switch/ternary/try-catch) to choose what is asserted.
assertions.evidence: 5 method(s) apply one uniform assertion pattern to all rows

assertions.text: Product prices and coupon rules are visible in the table via columns, @Description, or explicit setup.
assertions.evidence: Catalogue column shows prices e.g. '[Widget: 10.00]', and Coupon column shows 'PERCENT 20', 'FIXED 5.00', etc.

assertions.text: TypeConverter methods are used to convert map/string table values into domain objects; test method bodies contain only arrange-act-assert — no object construction from raw table values.
assertions.evidence: appliesCouponsToTheCart body: 'Cart cart = Cart.withItems(Map.of()).withActiveCouponCode(activeCouponBefore); CouponStore store = code -> Optional.ofNullable(couponInStore);' constructs objects from raw table values instead of using TypeConverters.

assertions.text: Coupon data is expressed in a single column with a @TypeConverter
assertions.evidence: Coupon In Store | ... | PERCENT 10 ... FIXED 5.00 ... PRODUCT Widget 3.00 — one column, @TypeConverter parseCoupon

assertions.text: Columns representing maps use standard TableTest map syntax
assertions.evidence: Catalogue | [Widget: 9.99] ... Cart Before | [:] ... Stock | [Widget: 5]

assertions.text: @Description not merely redundant with scenario names

assertions.text: Titles state what the code does, not an external fact
